chemistry-killer-10.s.s1.explain:
Step 1: Gas moles go from 4 (reactants) to 2 (product). The forward reaction is exothermic.
Step 2: (A) Decreasing volume raises pressure, so the equilibrium shifts toward fewer gas moles (forward) and NH3 increases.
(B) Raising temperature favours the endothermic reverse reaction, so NH3 decreases.
(C) At constant volume, adding Ar leaves the concentrations (partial pressures) of N2, H2, NH3 unchanged, so Q = K and nothing shifts; NH3 is unchanged.
(D) At constant pressure, adding Ar expands the volume and lowers all reactant and product concentrations, so the equilibrium shifts to the side with more gas moles (reverse) and NH3 decreases.
(E) Adding H2 makes Q < K, so the forward reaction proceeds and the amount of NH3 (mol) increases.
Step 3: NH3 increases in (A) and (E).
Answer: (A), (E) (b).
